nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The hearth glows low and steady, the way it has all season, and for once nobody is leaning towards it. Bertram has his notebook open on his knee and is looking at one very old line.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have found item twelve. It is the oldest one in the book. It says, in handwriting that is mostly mine, 'See the comet.' It was written in pencil, when I was eight.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: That is a very small item for such a very old list. What comet?

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: The one that passes over the Starlit Isles once every seventy-six years. I was put to bed early that night. I was told it was too late for a child to stay up. I have thought about it on and off ever since.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: When does it come back? Is it, sorry, is it soon?

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Bertram turns a page and holds it up. Someone, some time ago, has done a great deal of arithmetic in the margin and underlined the answer three times.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: It is due this winter. It will take about as long to reach as it takes a very slow tortoise to cross a river.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: A comet! A date! A deadline in the actual sky! Everybody pack! We leave at once! We leave yesterday!

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Chad. It is seventy-six years long. It has never once been in a hurry.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: And nothing here has a deadline, you said so yourself. This is just a very big appointment.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: ...A very big appointment that will not be rushed, at which I will arrive absolutely on time and perfectly calm.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I think I'd like to come. If that's all right. I haven't been anywhere yet, except here.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I still have the warm cup you gave me, you know. I've been drinking out of it for months.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I still have the little poker, you know. I keep it in my pocket. I haven't poked a single thing.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I still sit in the chair by the fire, you know. It's mine now, a bit. I hope that's all right.

nodes.prompt: What do you say to Bertram?

options.label: It is going to be wonderful.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: Thank you. I have waited seventy-six years to be told that, and I am pleased to find it was worth the wait.

options.label: We will get you there.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: We will. I have already begun the list. I am on page two and it is not yet lunch.

options.label: What is item thirteen?

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: Ah. Item thirteen is 'ask what item thirteen is'. I wrote it when I was eight and I have never worked out why.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Right! Maple, the list. Juno, boots. Bertram, a very warm hat. Pip, the map. And I will bring the cape and a quiet, dignified attitude.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The hall has become a luggage shop. There are bags on the Duck Mat, bags on the bench and, for reasons nobody has yet explained, one bag on the ceiling.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Item one: socks, two pairs. Item two: a flask. Item three: a spare flask in case the first flask has opinions.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I have packed the cape, three capes, a cape for the cape, a rope and a drum.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: You will not need a drum.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: A drum is an emotional support instrument. I will be carrying it myself.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: Should I bring the notebook? I started one. It's not like Bertram's. It only has five items.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Five is a great number. Mine had one for a whole month and it said 'ask where the Duck Mat is'.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Biscuit has been quietly missing for some time. He is eventually discovered inside the largest bag, sitting very still, with a small sausage and the air of a dog who has understood exactly what is going on.

nodes.speaker: biscuit
nodes.text: Woof.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: He has packed himself. That is, frankly, the most organised thing anyone has done in this hall all week.

options.label: A warm layer, and a snack for later.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: Layers and a snack. I want that on a sign. It is the entire art of travelling in four words and a comma.

options.label: Something small from home.

reply.speaker: juno
reply.text: That's what I'm bringing too. The cup. It weighs hardly anything and it makes everywhere feel a bit like here.

options.label: Nothing at all. I will borrow.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: Magnificent! A traveller of pure trust! Take my second cape. Take my third. Take the drum.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: Do not take the drum.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At the doorway Maple stops and looks at the whole untidy heap. She does not sigh. She has, over the years, stopped sighing at things she is fond of.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Rest is training, and so is packing slowly. We leave in the morning. Nobody has to be anywhere before the kettle.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: At your own pace, everyone! That is the rule! Mostly I mean mine, but yours too!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The road to the Starlit Isles is not the shortest. It is, however, the one that goes back through everywhere, and nobody has the heart to suggest another.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I heard you were passing. The light is lit, the fleet is in, and I have slept eleven hours. I have also brought a present.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: She holds out a small brass lamp with a glass the colour of honey. A flame is already burning in it, steady and low.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: It is a little piece of the great lamp. It will not go out. Bertram, this is for the dark parts of the road.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have never been given a lamp before. I would like it recorded that it is a great deal heavier than a notebook and ever so much more welcome.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: Is it always like this? People just give you things, on the way?

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Not always! It helps if you once said hello at a very dull moment in the past. Wren. Nice to see you rested.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I am practically unrecognisable. I go to bed when the sun goes. It is shocking how much more day there is in the day.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The next stop is a hut at the snow line, where a stove has been going for longer than anyone has counted, and a sign on the door says STOP HERE in careful paint.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: There is soup. There is always soup. I made a pot for sixty and then I made a smaller pot, because I thought you might be hungry in a smaller way.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: I came down my steps for this. Nine landings, and I stopped at every one. It took the whole morning, and I enjoyed all of it.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: I have brought you this, Bertram. It is a mug. It does not have a lid, because it is meant to be finished.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: A mug to finish. Yes. I should like to finish a great many things. I have been collecting them.

nodes.prompt: What do you take from the road?

options.label: A spoonful of soup, for the way.

reply.speaker: hush
reply.text: A spoonful is the correct amount. It is exactly enough to know that there is more.

options.label: The hut's sign, in my head.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: 'Stop here.' It is the best thing anyone has ever painted on a door. Take it with you, and use it at once and often.

options.label: A good long look at everyone.

reply.speaker: juno
reply.text: That's what I'm doing. I've only been here a short while and I want to remember how everybody looks when they are glad.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: On! To the next! To the dunes and the Sphinx and the Worm! At the speed of a leisurely walk!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At the edge of the known map there is a river, and on the river there is a ferry, and on the ferry there is a tortoise who looks as though he has been expecting them for about four hundred years.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: The ferry leaves when it leaves.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Sedge! Old friend! When does it leave?

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: When you are all aboard and the tea is poured.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: It's what he said the first time, when I came to the coast. I thought it was a joke. It's actually just the truth.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I've never been on a boat. Is it, how is it? Does it go quickly?

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: It goes at the speed of a river. Which is to say, it arrives.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I should like that on my list. 'Go at the speed of a river.' I shall tick it off the moment we land.

nodes.prompt: How do you spend the crossing?

options.label: Watching the water.

reply.speaker: sedge
reply.text: Good. The water has a great deal to say, if nobody interrupts it.

options.label: Looking up, for the first stars.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: Yes. I have been looking up for seventy-six years. I never get bored of it. Come and look with me, {hero}.

options.label: Sitting with Sedge, saying nothing.

reply.speaker: sedge
reply.text: Hm. You are very good company. It takes some people decades to learn to say nothing well.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The ferry slides away from the bank with no more fuss than a leaf. On the far shore, so faint it might be a smudge on the evening, a line of small lights floats a little above the water.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: Those are the islands. Those are really them. They look like somebody left a lot of lanterns out to dry.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: The Isles are not far. Nothing is far, if you are not in a hurry. It is the rule of my whole profession.

chapters.title: Moths, Cats and One Large Turtle

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The Starlit Isles are exactly as they look from a distance, only more so. The grass is silver, the paths are made of small flat clouds, and everything makes a faint sound like a very pleased kettle.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I thought it'd be scary. It's actually the calmest place I've ever been. Even the wind says 'pardon me'.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A large moth settles on Chad's shoulder, with a lantern glowing in its belly. It looks at him for a long time and then, apparently satisfied, goes to sit on the drum.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: It has chosen the drum. It knows. It knows the drum has meaning.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A cat the colour of twilight pads over, leaving a very faint trail of sparkle, and sits in front of Juno with the dignity of a diplomat. She holds out a hand. The cat considers it, and then, with great ceremony, leans.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: Oh. Oh, hello. You're warm. You're, hello. Is this a yes?

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: That is a yes. I have known a number of cats, and that was a signed and witnessed yes.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Behind them, very slowly, a hill stands up. It has a shell. It has a small, kind face. There are stars on its back, and some of them are joined by faint lines.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It is the Star Turtle. It looks at the little group for a long moment and then lowers its head, like a very large person bowing in a very small doorway.

nodes.prompt: How do you greet the creatures of the Isles?

options.label: With a slow bow.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: That's what I'd do. It seems to understand it. It's bowing back, a bit slower, so we don't feel rushed.

options.label: By sitting down with them.

reply.speaker: juno
reply.text: That's the best idea. Everything is easier when you're at the same height as it.

options.label: By asking what they are waiting for.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: Ah. That is the right question. I have a feeling the answer is the same as mine.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Every one of them, the moth, the cat, the turtle, the hundred small lights in the grass, has turned to look at the same patch of sky. They have been waiting too. Nobody here is in a hurry. The waiting is the thing itself.

nodes.speaker: biscuit
nodes.text: Woof.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Biscuit agrees. He always does, but this time it counts.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: On the highest island there is a very bright light, sitting on the grass with its arms around its knees, and a crown slightly askew. It is, quite clearly, trying not to be seen.

nodes.speaker: comet
nodes.text: Go away. No. Do not go away. But do not look at me. I am not supposed to be here for three days.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Your Majesty! I am Chad, guildmaster, and I would like to say that I am a tremendous admirer of arriving on time.

nodes.speaker: comet
nodes.text: That is the whole problem. I have arrived on time for seventy-six years, and this time I came early. I looked at the road and I thought, what if I am late, and I went too fast, and now I am here, and nothing is ready.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I think everything is ready. The moths are ready. The cat is ready. There's a turtle with the whole sky on its back.

nodes.speaker: comet
nodes.text: But I am three days early. A king is not three days early. A king is on the dot.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: May I say something? I have waited seventy-six years for you, and I have never once minded that you took your time. I should not mind three days at all. I would be glad of the company.

nodes.speaker: comet
nodes.text: ...You would?

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The light turns slowly, and for the first time shows its face. It is round and rather pale and has the look of somebody who has not slept properly since a previous century.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Stay right where you are, Your Majesty. Rest is training. You have been going for seventy-six years. Sit. We will bring tea.

nodes.prompt: What do you say to the Comet King?

options.label: Early is only another way to arrive.

reply.speaker: comet
reply.text: Early is only another way to arrive. I shall put that on a flag. I have a great many flags.

options.label: Nobody minds. We are glad you came.

reply.speaker: comet
reply.text: Glad. That is a word I do not hear very often, on my long road. It is a very good word. I should like some more of it.

options.label: Would you like to stay with us until it is time?

reply.speaker: comet
reply.text: Yes. Yes, I should. I have never stayed anywhere. I have only ever passed.

nodes.speaker: comet
nodes.text: I have an idea. I will not pass over tonight. I will not cross the sky until you are all rested and ready. A king may do that. A king may be as slow as his guests like.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Your Majesty. Truly. You are my favourite king.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: There is a small fire, the low red kind. There are blankets and a flask and, a little way off, a king who has lain down with his crown over his eyes and is almost certainly asleep.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: I have checked the list. There is nothing left on it. I have not been here before, and I find I do not mind in the slightest.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I want to say something. If I could tell the me who walked in, who was so sure everybody knew what they were doing, I'd say: the wall counts. And so do you.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I'd tell the me at the door that it's fine to be nervous. And that someone will have the kettle on. They really will.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: I would tell mine to stop counting for a minute and sit down. It would not listen. I would sit beside it anyway.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: And I would say to the boy who was put to bed early: it is all right. It was only a long way off. It was always going to be worth the wait.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I would tell the Chad who arrived with a very big cape and no idea what he was doing that he did start at Level 1, like everyone. And that it turned out all right. And that the cape was too long.

nodes.prompt: What would you tell the person you were at the start?

options.label: You do not have to be good at it yet.

reply.speaker: juno
reply.text: Yes. That's the one I needed. I think I needed it more than anything.

options.label: Keep going at your own pace. It all adds up.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: At your own pace. It adds up, slowly, in the background, the way interest does. I keep a column for it.

options.label: Look up sometimes.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: Look up sometimes. Item one hundred and twelve. I shall write it in ink.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Nothing here has a deadline, even the comet. It's just waiting for us to be ready.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: One by one they lie back in the silver grass. The fire ticks. Somewhere a moth settles on a drum with a faint, contented thump. For a long time nobody says anything, which is the best thing anyone could have said.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: Everything's very big. And I'm very small. And it doesn't feel bad at all.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: No. It feels like belonging to something. Good night, everyone. Good night, sky.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The sky does not warn anyone. It simply, very quietly, begins to glow along one edge, the way a window does when somebody in the next room turns on a lamp.

nodes.speaker: comet
nodes.text: I am ready now. I would like to say I have rested, and that I have never been so well prepared for a journey in my entire very long life.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: Then let us all be quiet and look.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: He rises in a long, bright arc, trailing a tail of blue light across the whole dark width of the world. It is slow. It is gentle. It is, without any exaggeration, the most beautiful thing any of them has ever seen.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: Oh. Oh, it's really there. It's actually there.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I can't believe it's so quiet. You'd think it'd be louder.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I had prepared a speech with a goose in it. I find I have nothing to say at all. This is a first.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Bertram takes out his notebook. His hands are not quite steady. He finds item twelve, in the pencil of a boy of eight, and, slowly, with a pen that has been in his pocket the whole journey, he draws a tick.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: There. It is done. It took seventy-six years and an extra eleven weeks of packing, and I would not change a minute.

nodes.prompt: What do you do as the comet passes?

options.label: Stand beside Bertram.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: Thank you. It is a great thing, to be next to somebody at the moment a very old wish comes true.

options.label: Make a wish of your own.

reply.speaker: juno
reply.text: I'm doing that too. I won't say what. It's a small one, and it's already coming true.

options.label: Just look, with everything you have.

reply.speaker: comet
reply.text: Yes. That is what I am for. It is all I ever hoped anybody would do.

nodes.speaker: comet
nodes.text: I shall be back in seventy-six years. I would be delighted if there were a chair for me. I will bring the early arrival, and a very good reason.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: There will be a chair. There will be a very good chair, and it will be next to Juno's, and a kettle will be on.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The road home is shorter than the road there, as roads home always are. The hall is dark, except for one low red line in the grate, which has been there the whole time.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: The hearth has held. Nobody fed it. It has been keeping itself quite well, thank you.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I think I get it now. All of it. It's not about getting there. It's about being the sort of person who goes.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: And there's a chair by the fire for whoever turns up next. There always is.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have a new list. It has only one item. Item one: whatever comes next. I do not know what it is. I am delighted.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Move however you like, rest when you need to, and always leave the kettle on. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Have fun with it, the way you said you would, and bring a comet, or a friend. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Stay curious, the way you did from the very first day. There is always one more sky. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Far away a bell rings, a lamp winks, a chime sings, a table is laid and a small fire is kept. And somewhere very high, a king drifts on, taking his time, at his own pace, towards a chair that will be waiting seventy-six years from now.
